content.title: USPS Holidays in 2026: When is the Post Office Closed?
content.text: U.S. Postal Service Holidays in 2026: Is the Post Office Open on Memorial Day? Get services online even when there’s no mail delivery and post offices are closed Andy Markowitz and Phil Pruitt, Published December 26, 2024 / Updated April 10, 2026 The U.S. Postal Service observes 11 official holidays annually, including Memorial Day. Post offices will be closed on Monday, May 25, and the Postal Service will not deliver regular mail or packages on that date. Here are the Postal Service holidays for 2026: New Year’s Day: Thursday, Jan. 1Martin Luther King Jr. Day: Monday, Jan. 19Presidents’ Day: Monday, Feb. 16Memorial Day: Monday, May 25Juneteenth National Independence Day: Friday, June 19Independence Day: Saturday, July 4Labor Day: Monday, Sept. 7Columbus Day: Monday, Oct. 12Veterans Day: Wednesday, Nov. 11Thanksgiving: Thursday, Nov. 26Christmas: Friday, Dec. 25 Even when brick-and-mortar facilities are closed, some post office services are available online 24/7, including on holidays. With a USPS.com account, you can order stamps, print shipping labels, order boxes and other mail supplies, and request package pickups. Stamps are also sold at most major supermarkets, pharmacies and office supply stores, which are open on some federal holidays. FedEx and UPS holidays Other major delivery companies set their own schedules and operate partially or in full on some federal holidays. FedEx and UPS do not pick up or deliver on Memorial Day except through their services for urgent and critical deliveries. Their retail locations may be closed or operate on modified schedules; check with your local FedEx Office or UPS Store for details. Video: 3 Surprising Things You Never Knew About the Post Office Andy Markowitz is an AARP senior writer and editor covering Social Security and retirement. He is a former editor of the Prague Post and Baltimore City Paper. Phil Pruitt is an AARP writer and editor focusing on Social Security. He is a former editor at Scripps News and Yahoo News and was on the start-up staff at USA Today, where he held numerous editing positions. Most Popular Most Popular
